record.title: The Dry Tree
record.premise: On the road to Jal-Veesa the freed stranger picks Sithis' beard from under the crocodiles at Reed-Sill Weir for the town's sick Hist, and Vosh-Leera tells them that they now work for the Toh-Reel-Ka.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 2 and §2. Starts as MN01 ends, with the player freed and sent to Vosh-Leera. The player picks Sithis' beard below Reed-Sill Weir, past or through two young crocodiles (fight, shoot from the log walk, or sneak), and brings it to Weeltul, Jal-Veesa's tree-minder, at the Hist pool. She shows the sick tree (dry dark bark, a closed scar, a cooling egg-pool), makes a poultice that warms the pool but does not open the scar, says what the town loses if the tree dies, and has the player lay a hand on the bark for the tree's blessing (the town's own shrine-blessing: waterbreathing, or resist poison for an Argonian). Vosh-Leera then tells the player who they now work for, how the An-Xileel used Lilmoth's mad tree to call Umbriel down, and why a stranger with no kin was chosen; she pays 50 gold and asks the player back to her house for a second task, which starts MN03. The jal-veesa-minder of the line is named Weeltul here.

truth.what: Jal-Veesa's Hist fell sick. Its bark dried and darkened, its scar closed and gives no sap, and its egg-pool has cooled. Weeltul cannot find a cause. Sithis' beard, laid in the pool as a poultice, warms the water for a while.

Vosh-Leera, root-herald of the town, began to pass what she heard to a Toh-Reel-Ka handler, without asking what was done with it. This season the order told her to find a stranger with no kin in the work gangs and free them, since such a stranger makes a cheap and useful spy; she chose the player from the barge's list.

The An-Xileel, who then ruled Black Marsh, used Lilmoth's mad Hist to call the flying city Umbriel down on the marsh; its dead killed Lilmoth's people. The An-Xileel fell. The Xeech-Leel rose by being their opposite, and in 4E 98 to 100 made the Toh-Reel-Ka so that no tree and nobody allied with a tree could do it again.

facts.claim: Jal-Veesa's Hist is sick: its bark is dry and dark, its scar has closed and its egg-pool is cooling; nobody knows why.
If the tree dies, no egg in its pools will hatch again and the town has no future.

The player now works for the Toh-Reel-Ka, "the Secret Warriors", the elite order of the Xeech-Leel who rule the province, made after Umbriel so that no tree and nobody allied with one can turn on the marsh again.
The order frees strangers with no kin from the gangs because such a stranger makes a useful spy and a cheap one; the player is not special.
In 4E 48 the An-Xileel used Lilmoth's mad tree to call the flying city Umbriel down; its dead killed Lilmoth's people.

topics.label: Dralin Uveran said you wanted me.
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera, if the player comes before the moss is given. Tells: she did; she is Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa. But Weeltul, the tree-minder at the pool in the middle of the town, needs that moss first; bring it from the weir to her, let her show you the tree, then come back and Vosh-Leera will tell you what you were freed for. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Sithis' beard for?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: a long grey moss that hangs over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir. Laid in an egg-pool as a poultice it warms the water for a few days. The crocodiles lie under the weir where the moss hangs; a hunter shoots them from the log walk, and a careful one picks the moss from the bank behind them. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is a Hist?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: the great thinking tree every Argonian town stands round; this one is the tall grey tree in the pool behind her, Jal-Veesa's own. Its bark should be pale and soft; feel how dry it is now. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: she is Weeltul, tree-minder of Jal-Veesa: she tends the town's Hist, keeps its egg-pool and draws its sap; every hatchling of the town comes to her on its naming day. She is waiting on Sithis' beard from the weir. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: I brought Sithis' beard from the weir.
topics.intent: Weeltul. Checks: hasItem [thing.mn02.sithis-beard, 1]. Tells: she takes it and lays it in the pool as a poultice. She shows the player the tree: its bark should be pale grey and soft and is dry and dark; its scar, the one place in the bark where she draws a little sap, has closed and gives nothing; its egg-pool, where the town's eggs lie among the roots, is cooling. The moss warms the water for a few days but does not open the scar. She does not know the cause; no minder on the river does. If the tree dies, no egg in its pools will ever hatch again, and in a generation Jal-Veesa is empty. She asks the player to lay a hand on the bark at the pool's edge: a tree gives its blessing to those its people trust, and the player brought the moss (the town's shrine-blessing: waterbreathing for a time, or, for an Argonian, who already breathes water, resist poison). Vosh-Leera is waiting in her house on the bank. Does: sets stage 30, whose start takes the moss.

topics.label: Tell me about the eggs.
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: Argonian eggs are laid in the pool among a Hist's roots, and the tree keeps them warm and alive through its roots. If a tree's bond with its eggs is cut, the unborn die in the shell. A village whose tree dies has no future: nothing in its pools will hatch again. This pool is cooling; she has turned the eggs twice today. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the sap?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: sap is what a Hist bleeds, amber-coloured and thick. A hatchling licks its tree's sap on its naming day, and the sap shapes its body for life. Drunk, it brings visions the tree sends, of far places; minders drink a little to ask the trees a question. It makes a fighter stronger for a time, which is why some steal it. In the old days the trees made it hard as stone, amber, but no tree does that now. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the scar?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: every Hist has one place in its bark, low on the trunk, where its minder cuts a little and the tree gives sap there and nowhere else; that is the scar. A healthy tree's scar weeps sap when it is opened. A sick tree's scar closes over and gives nothing. Jal-Veesa's closed this season. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What was Umbriel?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells, in a line or two: a flying city that came down on Lilmoth long ago, called by the An-Xileel through Lilmoth's mad tree; every minder is taught it as a warning of what a tree can be made to do. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: root-herald of Jal-Veesa: she speaks for the town's elders and its tree to anyone from outside, Dunmer buyers and Stormhold's halls and gang-masters among them. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Why did you have me freed?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera, in her house, privately: nobody names the order aloud in company. Tells: the player has seen the tree. Trees are falling sick, one at a time, along the river, and nobody knows why. The people she answers to want it found. They are the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Secret Warriors: the elite order of the Xeech-Leel, the People of the New Beginning, who have ruled the province since the An-Xileel fell. In 4E 48 the An-Xileel, who ruled then, used the mad Hist of Lilmoth to call down the flying city Umbriel, and its dead killed Lilmoth's people. The Xeech-Leel made the Toh-Reel-Ka so that no tree, and nobody allied with a tree, can ever turn on the marsh like that again. They comb the work gangs for strangers with no kin and no ties, because such a stranger makes a useful spy and a cheap one; she chose the player off the barge's list. Nobody in the marsh is owed a reason. They pay, and they give work. She gives the player fifty gold and asks them to come back to her, here, for a second task. Does: sets stage 90. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: Tell me about the Toh-Reel-Ka.
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: Toh-Reel-Ka is Jel for "Secret Warriors": toh, secret, as in xal-toh, sacred secret, and reel-ka, warrior. They are the Xeech-Leel's order of spies and guards, made in the Void Nights, when the moons vanished and the province feared its trees were turning again. They watch the trees and anyone who seeks a tree's power, and they answer only to the Xeech-Leel's council at Helstrom. They wear no mark; their handlers keep quiet houses in the cities; people like her pass on what they hear. She has never asked what they do with it. Nobody names them aloud in company, and neither should the player. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are the Xeech-Leel?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: Xeech-Leel means the People of the New Beginning: Xeech, the planting month, and leel, people. They took the province in the generations after Umbriel by being everything the An-Xileel were not. Their first promise is that no faction may speak alone with a tree; they swore to govern in the open, and their council sits at Helstrom. They hold the old forts, roads and tolls through their Archwardens; inland the towns and tribes run themselves, as Jal-Veesa does. People call them "the Wardens", or "the New Beginning". Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What was Umbriel?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: in 4E 48 the An-Xileel, who ruled Black Marsh then, sang to Lilmoth's Hist in secret until it went mad, and through it called down Umbriel, a flying city, onto the marsh. The city's dead killed the people of Lilmoth. The An-Xileel fell for it and their name went with them. That is why the province fears a tree turned to a faction's use, and why the order exists. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

record.premise: A stranger sent up the river on an Owing barge gives the gang's cook their name and trade in the barge's hold, and is freed on the landing by a sour gang-master on an order from Vosh-Leera of Jal-Veesa.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 1 (passed by the owner, 2026-11-17) and §1. The game opens in the hold of the Owing barge moored at Ashgate Landing; the hold's door is locked. Okeeh, the gang's cook, asks the player's name (the "player's name set from a conversation" block: the stage after her line opens the game's own name entry) and their trade (a profession as in Morrowind: each answer sets a stage that raises five skills by five; one answer lets the player name their own five, one at a time, each pick a stage that raises that skill by five). When the trade is given the door is unlocked from outside. Dralin Uveran, the gang-master, speaks first on the landing (the quest's one speaks-first line), says the player's name was struck from his roll this morning on Vosh-Leera's order, and sends them to her house in Jal-Veesa, passing on the tree-minder's request for Sithis' beard from Reed-Sill Weir on the way. The player's pack holds two lockpicks. MN02 starts on this quest's stage 90 and carries the markers on the weir's moss and on Vosh-Leera's door. The side quest What the Herald Sent is left out: the main quest only. Okeeh and Dralin first answer the line's shared topics Hist, Jal-Veesa and the Owing.

truth.what: The barge moored in the river pool below the camp. Dralin locked the new gang in the hold to sleep, as he does with every new gang until their names are on his roll.

Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa, came down the road with an order that the stranger's months be struck from the roll. Dralin cannot refuse a root-herald. He struck the name and lost a cutter he had paid for. She did not say why, and went back to Jal-Veesa. (She acts for the Toh-Reel-Ka, who comb the gangs for strangers with no kin; the player learns that in MN02.)
Weeltul, Jal-Veesa's tree-minder, has asked every gang on the river for Sithis' beard, a grey moss that hangs over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir, to warm her sick tree's cooling egg-pool.

facts.claim: The player is in the hold of an Owing barge moored at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp on the river west of Loriasel, in Black Marsh.
The Owing is the marsh's sentence: months of owed work in place of a cell. The gang is here to serve its months cutting reed.
The hold's door is locked from outside until the gang-master takes the new gang's names.
The player's name was struck from the gang-master's roll this morning, on an order brought by Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa: they owe no months and are free.
Vosh-Leera wants to see the player at her house in Jal-Veesa, a town up the road to the east.
Jal-Veesa's tree-minder wants Sithis' beard, a grey moss hanging over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir, which is on the road to the town.
A Hist is a great thinking tree, the size of a tower, with pale grey bark, roots standing out of the water and a pool of eggs at its foot; every Argonian village is built round one.

This is the hold of an Owing barge moored at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp in Black Marsh, and the gang here are sent to cut reed for the months they owe. I gave her my name. I'm to tell her what my trade was. The door stays locked until the gang-master takes our names.

topics.label: Where am I?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: "You're in the hold of the work barge, moored at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp on the river west of Loriasel. This is Black Marsh, the Argonians' country." The barge brought this gang up from the sea to serve the Owing: months of owed work given by the marsh in place of a cell, served here cutting reed for the mat-makers of Stormhold. She is Okeeh, the gang's cook. The door is locked from outside, as it is for every new gang, until the gang-master, a Dunmer named Dralin Uveran, takes their names onto his roll; it will not be long. She does not know the player's face, and asks their name (a question; its answer is topic.mn01-name). Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: My name? I'll tell you.
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: she listens and says the name back, so she can shout it at mealtimes. Does: sets stage 20, whose start opens the game's name entry; then she asks what the player did before the marsh caught them: "Every gang has a fighter, a hunter, a thief and someone who knows a poultice. What were you?" (a question; its answers are the seven trade topics). Checks: nothing.

topics.label: What do you mean, my trade?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: what the player did before is what they will be good at here; she lists the answers she has heard and what each is good for: a warrior (One-Handed, Two-Handed, Block, Heavy Armor, Smithing), a hunter (Archery, Sneak, Light Armor, Alchemy, One-Handed), a thief (Sneak, Lockpicking, Pickpocket, Speech, Light Armor), a battlemage (Destruction, Alteration, Conjuration, One-Handed, Heavy Armor), a healer (Restoration, Alchemy, Illusion, Alteration, Speech), a nightblade (Illusion, Sneak, One-Handed, Destruction, Light Armor), or "none of those: name me your own five". Whatever the player says, those five come a little easier from today. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: I was a warrior.
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: then the player can carry a blade and a shield; she has heard noise on the landing. Does: sets stage 31 (One-Handed, Two-Handed, Block, Heavy Armor and Smithing each raised by five; the door unbarred). Checks: nothing.

topics.label: I was a hunter.
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: there is game enough in the reeds for a hunter. Does: sets stage 32 (Archery, Sneak, Light Armor, Alchemy and One-Handed each raised by five; the door unbarred). Checks: nothing.

topics.label: I was a thief.
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: she will count her spoons. Does: sets stage 33 (Sneak, Lockpicking, Pickpocket, Speech and Light Armor each raised by five; the door unbarred). Checks: nothing.

topics.label: I was a battlemage.
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: a mage with a blade, and on a reed gang. Does: sets stage 34 (Destruction, Alteration, Conjuration, One-Handed and Heavy Armor each raised by five; the door unbarred). Checks: nothing.

topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: the gang will want the player when the reed cuts their hands. Does: sets stage 35 (Restoration, Alchemy, Illusion, Alteration and Speech each raised by five; the door unbarred). Checks: nothing.

topics.label: What is the Owing?
topics.intent: Okeeh (and, by his own row, Dralin from stage 90). Tells: the Owing is the marsh's sentence. Black Marsh's own towns keep no jails; a debtor, a thief or a stranger who broke the peace is given months of owed work instead, and a broker sells those months to a gang-master like Dralin, who feeds the gang and works them until the months are served. Most of this gang owe six months or a year. Nobody counts a stranger's months kindly. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the Owing?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: months of work owed instead of a cell; he buys them from the broker at Stormhold and his cutters work them off on the reed beds. The player's months were bought and are gone now, and that is his loss, not theirs. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is a Hist?
topics.intent: Okeeh, an Argonian. Tells: a Hist is one of the great trees of Black Marsh, and they think. A Hist is as tall as a tower, with pale grey bark and roots standing up out of the water, and a pool at its foot where the eggs lie among the roots. Every Argonian village is built round its own tree. On a hatchling's naming day it licks its tree's sap, and the sap shapes it for life; her own tree is far to the south, and she still dreams of it. All the trees are joined at the root, so what one knows the others can know. An Argonian with a hand on the bark can hear them. They are not just trees: if a village's tree dies, no egg in its pools will hatch again. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is a Hist?
topics.intent: Dralin, a Dunmer. Tells: the Argonians' great trees, grey-barked and as big as towers, with an egg-pool at the foot; every village stands round one, and they say the trees think. He has seen men stand with a hand on one for an hour. Jal-Veesa's is the tall grey tree in the pool at the middle of the town, and it has looked poorly since the rains. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Jal-Veesa?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: the town of the Veesa-Teeleel, the Sedge-Wardens, east up the road: stilt houses on mud banks round a pool, boat-lanes cut through the sedge, mats and fish drying on racks. The tall grey tree standing in the pool at the middle of the town is its Hist. She buys the gang's dried fish there. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Jal-Veesa?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: the Sedge-Wardens' town, east up the road past Reed-Sill Weir: stilt houses round a pool with their Hist in the middle. Its elders answer to nobody in Stormhold, and its root-herald, Vosh-Leera, speaks for them to outsiders. Her house is in the town; any warden will point to it. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: the gang's cook; she owes no months, she is paid, and she has cooked for Dralin's gangs four seasons. She sells dried fish and lamp oil from her stall by the hut. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Hara-Jeel. Tells: a reed-cutter of this gang, owing a year for a debt at Stormhold; he came up on the barge beside the player and does not know them either. The door opens when the gang-master wants it to. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: (speaks first) You. Off the barge.
topics.intent: Dralin Uveran, a step from the hold's door as the player comes out. Tells: he is Dralin Uveran, gang-master here. The player's name is not on his roll: it was struck this morning, before they cut a single reed, on an order brought down the road by Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa, the one who speaks for that town's elders and its tree to outsiders. He cannot refuse a root-herald. "You must have friends in high places." He paid for the player's months and has lost them. She wants the player at her house in Jal-Veesa, east up the road; he does not know why and does not care to. While they are going that way: the town's tree-minder has asked every gang on the river for Sithis' beard, a grey moss that hangs over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir, the weir-wardens' camp where the road meets the creek. Mind the crocodiles under the weir. Does: sets stage 90. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: the gang-master of Ashgate Landing, a Dunmer of Stormhold who buys Owing months and works them off on the reed. He has nothing more for the player. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who is Vosh-Leera?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: Jal-Veesa's root-herald. A root-herald speaks for a town's elders and its tree to anyone from outside, so an order from her is the town's order. She walked down this morning, gave the order and went back. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Sithis' beard?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: a long grey moss that hangs from the trees over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir, the first camp on the road east. Tree-minders use it for something; Jal-Veesa's minder wants it badly. There are crocodiles under the weir where the wardens throw their offal; kill them, shoot them from the log walk on top of the weir, or keep out of their sight. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.
